latestRelease.title: v1.65.0/v0.159.0
latestRelease.notes:
### Images and binaries here: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-releases/releases/tag/v0.159.0

## End User Changelog

### 💡 Enhancements 💡

- `pkg/exporterhelper`: Add the `pkg.exporterhelper.queueBatchEnabled` feature gate (#14038, #13582, #12022)
  When enabled, the batch settings returned by `NewDefaultQueueConfig()` have
  `batch::enabled` true. See [migration RFC](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/main/docs/rfcs/batching-migration.md#phase-1).
  

### 🧰 Bug fixes 🧰

- `pkg/exporterhelper`: Record `otelcol_exporter_queue_batch_send_size` and `otelcol_exporter_queue_batch_send_size_bytes` after batching, and add `otelcol_exporter_enqueue_size` and `otelcol_exporter_enqueue_size_bytes` for enqueue-time sizes. (#14674)
  Previously the batch send size histograms were recorded at enqueue time (`Offer`), so they
  measured incoming request sizes rather than the post-batching request handed to the
  downstream sender. Those histograms are now recorded in the obs report sender.
  The previous enqueue-time measurements are preserved under the new
  `otelcol_exporter_enqueue_size` and `otelcol_exporter_enqueue_size_bytes` metrics for
  queue sizing. Users with the exporter batcher enabled will observe different values for
  `otelcol_exporter_queue_batch_send_size*`.
  `otelcol_exporter_queue_batch_send_size` and `otelcol_exporter_queue_batch_send_size_bytes`
  are now only recorded when `sending_queue::batch` is configured; they will not appear at all
  for exporters that do not enable batching.
  
- `pkg/scraperhelper`: Use `{record}` instead of `{datapoint}` as the unit of the log record and profile record scraper metrics (#15730)
  Affects `otelcol_scraper_scraped_log_records`, `otelcol_scraper_errored_log_records`,
  `otelcol_scraper_scraped_profile_records` and `otelcol_scraper_errored_profile_records`.
  

<!-- previous-version -->

## API Changelog

### 🛑 Breaking changes 🛑

- `extension/zpages`: Make `confighttp.ServerConfig` a named field of `Config` instead of an embedded one. (#15308)
- `pkg/confighttp`: Make `configauth.Config` a named field of `AuthConfig` instead of an embedded one. (#15308)

### 💡 Enhancements 💡

- `pkg/config/configretry`: Migrate `BackOffConfig` to schema-based configuration generated by mdatagen. (#15502)
- `pkg/config/configtls`: Migrate `TLS` core types to schema-based configuration generated by mdatagen. (#15693)

signals.title: [confmap] is not preserving the original type when a slice of a map is unmarshalled
signals.text: ### Component(s) confmap ### What happened? **Describe the bug** When using an env variable with numerical values, example: `SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN=12345` ```` extensions: headers_setter: headers: - action: upsert key: X-SF-TOKEN from_context: X-SF-TOKEN default_value: "${SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN}" ```` the collector fails to start with the below error: ```` Error: failed to get config: cannot unmarshal the configuration: decoding failed due to the following error(s): error decoding 'extensions': error reading configuration for "headers_setter": decoding failed due to the following error(s): 'headers[0].default_value' expected type 'string', got unconvertible type 'int', value: '12345' ```` **Steps to reproduce** Set the env variable to `SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN=12345` and run contrib using a config like this: ```` extensions: headers_setter: headers: - action: upsert key: X-SF-TOKEN from_context: X-SF-TOKEN default_value: "${SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN}" receivers: hostmetrics: collection_interval: 10s scrapers: filesystem: memory: processors: batch: batch/out: metadata_keys: - X-SF-Token exporters: otlphttp: metrics_endpoint: https://ingest.us1.signalfx.com/v2/datapoint/otlp headers: X-SF-Token: "${SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN}" auth: authenticator: headers_setter service: telemetry: logs: level: "info" pipelines: metrics/internal: receivers: [hostmetrics] processors: [batch] exporters: [otlphttp] extensions: [headers_setter] ```` **What did you expect to see?** No error **What did you see instead?** Below error ```` Error: failed to get config: cannot unmarshal the configuration: decoding failed due to the following error(s): error decoding 'extensions': error reading configuration for "headers_setter": decoding failed due to the following error(s): 'headers[0].default_value' expected type 'string', got unconvertible type 'int', value: '12345' ```` What I believe is happening is that the confmap correctly handles maps and run each entry of the map into the `isStringyStructure`, however, when a config is made out of a slice of maps is used (like the case here), the decoder hooks do not run each entry of the slice into `isStringyStructure` . ### Collector version main ### Environment information ## Environment OS: (e.g., "Ubuntu 20.04") Compiler(if manually compiled): (e.g., "go 14.2") ### OpenTelemetry Collector configuration ```yaml extensions: headers_setter: headers: - X-SF-Token exporters: otlphttp: metrics_endpoint: https://ingest.us1.signalfx.com/v2/datapoint/otlp headers: X-SF-Token: "${SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN}" auth: authenticator: headers_setter service: telemetry: logs: level: "info" pipelines: metrics/internal: receivers: [hostmetrics] processors: [batch] exporters: [otlphttp] extensions: [headers_setter] ``` ### Log output ```shell ``` ### Additional context _No response_

signals.title: Components using sharedcomponent may emit invalid status sequences
signals.text: ### Component(s) https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/tree/main/internal/sharedcomponent ### Describe the issue you're reporting > [!IMPORTANT] > The effects of this issue are completely hidden by the status state machine discarding invalid status transitions. I'm filing it for reference, as it came up while working on #14282. Shared components need to report status differently than normal components to avoid duplication and race conditions. The [implementation](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/a1eb0cadf34bcbeb20d483e5f18e1da0325ba1f1/internal/sharedcomponent/sharedcomponent.go#L87) claims it does this, but in practice has several issues which are hidden by the [status finite state machine](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/80269724f45ae2b17bca7bb533d05c577b33aa8d/service/internal/status/status.go#L50). #### Component start and shutdown statuses are reported twice The implementation claims it takes over from the component graph, but this isn't true. `Graph.StartAll` [always reports](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/80269724f45ae2b17bca7bb533d05c577b33aa8d/service/internal/graph/graph.go#L427) `Starting`, `OK` and `PermanentError` if needed. This duplicates the statuses already reported by the sharedcomponent wrapper. #### The graph may report a Starting status after the actual component emits a different one Sharedcomponent starts the actual component on the first call to `Start()`, and the component will start running immediately, and can immediately report statuses. These are correctly routed and retained for components which are started later, but the graph will still emit `Starting` for those components - despite the component already running and emitting its own statuses. #### Permanent errors are only returned on the first call to `Start()` Subsequent calls return `nil`. Currently, this isn't a problem because the graph will abort on first error, but it will become a problem if we want to change that behavior in the future. ### Tip <sub>[React](https://github.blog/news-insights/product-news/add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) with 👍 to help prioritize this issue. Please use comments to provide useful context, avoiding `+1` or `me too`, to help us triage it. Learn more [here](https://opentelemetry.io/community/end-user/issue-participation/).</sub>

signals.title: [cmd/mdatagen] [filter] Allow wildcard patterns as a filtering option
signals.text: ### Component(s) cmd/mdatagen ### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe. The `filter` package has a config with two fields: `strict`, and `regexp`. This allows filtering based on string literals or Go regexes. This filter config could be used to address [the desire to mass enable/disable metrics in `MetricsBuilder`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/10074). But using a regex pattern is pretty cumbersome when OTel names are expected to be separated with `.`, which is a regex operator. ### Describe the solution you'd like The [Go metric SDK for Views accepts a simple wildcard pattern](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/blob/91fcbbd0066dba7163ee29f6a2eb7c17a49e0975/sdk/metric/view.go#L71-L77) only supporting `*` (multi-character) and `?` (single-character) wildcards. A new field could be added to filter called `pattern` that would accept this format in the same way. ### Describe alternatives you've considered We could stick to just allowing regexes. I suppose it wouldn't be the end of the world. Using this pattern would just be a significantly nicer config experience in my opinion. ### Additional context _No response_ ### Tip <sub>[React](https://github.blog/news-insights/product-news/add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) with 👍 to help prioritize this issue. signals.title: [processor/memorylimiter] Only send component status events when status changed
signals.text: ### Component(s) processor/memorylimiter ### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe. Now that `memory_limiter` processor reports component status, it can result in a lot of health check events being generated. An event is generated with each check, even when there is no change in status. This can create a lot of noise since the memory_limiter is typically running quite frequently (e.g. recommended default `check_interval` is 1s). This can increases load/impact on the downstream consumers of health events. https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/885b51bf8959315048480c9b1856c605a779b7ec/internal/memorylimiter/memorylimiter.go#L267-L275 ### Describe the solution you'd like Only report the health event status when the state has changed ### Describe alternatives you've considered _No response_ ### Additional context _No response_ ### Tip <sub>[React](https://github.blog/news-insights/product-news/add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) with 👍 to help prioritize this issue. signals.title: [confighttp] Move keepalive config into a dedicated optional section
signals.text: #### Description Move the keepalive-related options into a dedicated optional section. We go from: ```yaml endpoint: "http://localhost:4318" idle_conn_timeout: 90s max_idle_conns: 100 max_idle_conns_per_host: 10 ``` to: ```yaml endpoint: "http://localhost:4318" keepalive: idle_conn_timeout: 90s max_idle_conns: 100 max_idle_conns_per_host: 10 ``` The old configuration still exists and works. We fail validation if both are set. The implementation is somewhat complex and tries to minimize breakage across multiple scenarios. It proceeds by standardizing on the old, deprecated fields in `Unmarshal` and nulling the new section. See comments on the `Unmarshal` implementation and compatibility tests in `keepalive_compat_tests.go`. The most notable scenario that doesn't work goes like this: ```go cfg := NewDefaultClientConfig() conf.Unmarshal(cfg) cfg.KeepAlive = nil client := cfg.ToClient() ``` Keepalives will be enabled for such a client. This, and other limitations, exist as tests in `keepalive_compat_test.go`. Their intent is to show how a given implementation fares, in case somebody can come up with a better one. #### Link to tracking issue Fixes https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/14020 #### Testing Added unit tests for all the new functions and some more generic unmarshalling tests. I've also added compatibility tests in `keepalive_compat_test.go` which assert that typical use cases from contrib still work as expected, and also show the limitations of this approach. I'm open to dropping some of them after review, but I think they're very useful until we decide on an approach. <!--Describe the documentation added.--> #### Documentation Updated README and the config schema.
signals.author: swiatekm

signals.title: [exporter/otlp_http] Prevent retries when body parsing fails on successful HTTP exports
signals.text: ### Description Fixes an issue in the `otlp_http` exporter where successful (2xx) HTTP response bodies exceeding the 64kB limit (`maxHTTPResponseReadBytes`) triggered retry loops. To resolve this, any error encountered while reading or parsing a successful (2xx) response body is now wrapped and returned as a permanent error (`consumererror.NewPermanent(err)`). This ensures the exporter drops the batch and does not attempt to retry. ### Link to tracking issue Fixes #15386 ### Testing - Added a new unit test `TestPartialSuccess_responseBodyTooLarge` in `exporter/otlphttpexporter/otlp_test.go` verifying that a partial success response exceeding 64kB returns a permanent error. - Ran all package tests successfully using `go test -v ./...` and `make test`. - Ran linter validation successfully using `make lint`. ### Documentation No documentation changes are required. ### Authorship - [x] I, a human, wrote this pull request description myself.

signals.title: fix(service): prevent deadlock when reporting fatal errors during shutdown
signals.text: Ran into this while reviewing shutdown behavior for #9824. The problem is that during shutdown, startup, or config reload the collector control loop is not actively reading from asyncErrorChannel. If a component goroutine calls NotifyComponentStatusChange with a fatal error, the unbuffered channel send blocks forever, deadlocking the caller. I went with a non-blocking select (with default) rather than buffering the channel, because buffering would change the semantics for the normal running case and could mask real errors. With this approach the send succeeds when the control loop is listening, and is silently dropped otherwise, which is the safest behavior during shutdown. Not 100% sure if there is a better way to surface the dropped error, feedback welcome. Fixes #9824

The main reason for this release is compatibility with the new lychee `0.24.x` release artifacts. Starting with lychee `v0.24.0`, the archive layout changed, and the `lychee` binary may now be packaged inside a subdirectory. `lychee-action` now detects that layout automatically, so users can upgrade without changing their workflows. If you use: ```yaml uses: lycheeverse/lychee-action@v2 ``` you will get the new version once the floating `v2` tag has been updated. If you pin exact versions, update to: ```yaml uses: lycheeverse/lychee-action@v2.9.0 ``` #### What’s new from lychee `v0.24.x` ##### Better diagnostics lychee now reports line and column numbers for detected links. This makes broken link reports easier to act on, especially in larger documentation sites or generated reports. ##### Text fragment checking lychee can now check URL text fragments, such as links containing `#:~:text=...`. This helps catch links that point to a valid page but no longer points to the intended highlighted text. ##### Sitemap support lychee can now read `sitemap.xml` inputs. This is useful for checking published websites or generated documentation sites where the sitemap is the easiest source of URLs to validate. ##### JUnit output lychee now supports JUnit output. This makes it easier to integrate link checking results with CI systems and test reporting tools that understand JUnit XML. ##### Redirect and remap visibility lychee can now show redirects and remaps more clearly. This helps explain why a URL was checked as a different final URL and makes debugging link-checking behavior easier. ##### Multiple config files lychee now supports multiple configuration files and expanded config handling. This is useful for repositories that split documentation, website, or package-specific link-checking settings. ##### Timeout handling lychee can now accept timeouts explicitly. This gives users more control over how strict their link checks should be for flaky or slow endpoints. #### Fixes and reliability improvements ##### Fixed lychee `0.24.x` archive compatibility `lychee-action` now handles the new lychee release archive layout by detecting whether the `lychee` binary is inside a subdirectory. This fixes compatibility with lychee `0.24.x`. ##### More stable installation path The action now installs lychee into `$RUNNER_TEMP/lychee/bin` instead of `$HOME`. This avoids failures on runners where `$HOME` differs between composite action steps. In those environments, the action could add one directory to `PATH` but install the binary somewhere else, causing `lychee: command not found`. ##### Safer automatic lychee version updates The workflow that checks for new lychee releases now guards against `null` release versions before creating update PRs. This prevents invalid automated PRs such as “Update lycheeVersion to null”. ##### Dependency updates - Updated `actions/checkout` from `v6` to `v7` - Updated `actions/cache` from `v5` to `v6` #### Upstream lychee changelog For the full lychee changelog, see: - See [docs](https://codspeed.io/docs/instruments/cpu#estimating-cycles). ##### New: allocation exclusion Opt in to `exclude-allocations` to remove allocator time from benchmarks in Simulation mode and reduce variance. signals.title: feat: add support for identity compression algorithm in confighttp
signals.text: #### Description Per RFC 7231 3.1.2.2, `Content-Encoding: identity` is a valid header value that signifies no encoding/compression was used. The `httpContentDecompressor` previously rejected payloads with `Content-Encoding: identity` with a `400 Bad Request` because `"identity"` was not registered in the available decoders. This PR fixes the issue by mapping `"identity"` to act as a pass-through (identical to `""`) whenever uncompressed payloads are allowed. This also resolves a documented `// BUG:` in the `compression_test.go` suite. #### Link to tracking issue Fixes # #### Testing - Updated the `Mixed_Identity_ShouldAccept` test case in `compression_test.go` which previously expected a `400 Bad Request` (marked as a BUG) to correctly expect `200 OK`. - Ran `go test ./...` in `config/confighttp` and verified all tests pass. #### Documentation None needed. #### Authorship - [x] I, a human, wrote this pull request description myself.

signals.title: [chore][internal/e2e] Wait for the collector to be running before sending data
signals.text: #### Description `TestMetricStability` and `TestInternalTelemetry_ServiceInstanceID` treat a successful scrape of the telemetry `/metrics` endpoint as "the collector is ready". It is not. The meter provider — and with it the Prometheus HTTP server — is created in `service.New` ([`service.go:194`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/0ffbf34b9/service/service.go#L194)). The OTLP receiver only starts much later, in `service.Start` -> `Pipelines.StartAll` ([`service.go:274`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/0ffbf34b9/service/service.go#L274)). Between those two points `/metrics` answers `200` while nothing is listening on the OTLP port, so `waitMetricsReady` returns early and the following `sendTestData` fails with `connect: connection refused`. The window spans `CreateTracerProvider` and `graph.Build` ([`service.go:378`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/0ffbf34b9/service/service.go#L378)), which instantiates every component — cheap on a developer machine, expensive under `-race` on a loaded CI runner. The CI logs confirm this directly. In job `91217674049` the captured output for the failing subtest contains `Internal trace telemetry disabled` (logged by `CreateTracerProvider`, `service.go:209`) but no `Starting otelcol...` — the first line of `service.Start` — anywhere in the log. The collector was inside the window when the test sent data. The `cannot start pipelines: failed to start "otlp" receiver: listen tcp: lookup localhost: operation was canceled` line in #15492 is a consequence rather than the cause: `require.NoError` in `sendTestData` calls `FailNow`, which runs `runtime.Goexit`, which fires the `defer cancel()` — cancelling the context that `confignet.TCPAddrConfig.Listen` is resolving `localhost` under. This PR waits for `Collector.GetState() == StateRunning`, which is set after `service.Start` returns. That is a sound readiness signal because `ToListener(ctx)` is called synchronously inside `startHTTPServer` ([`otlp.go:171`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/0ffbf34b9/receiver/otlpreceiver/otlp.go#L171)) — only `Serve` is backgrounded — so the socket is bound and accepting before `Start` returns. It also surfaces a startup failure through a channel instead of logging it from a goroutine. The previous `t.Logf`/`assert.NoError` calls could run after the test had finished, which panics with `Log in goroutine after test has completed` and would mask the real error. The same defect and the same fix apply to `TestInternalTelemetry_ServiceInstanceID`, which showed up in the same CI sweep. #### Link to tracking issue Fixes #15492 #### Testing `TestMetricStability` accounted for 13 of the 20 most recent failed `build-and-test` runs at the time of writing, across both subtests. That both subtests fail rules out the hardcoded `8888` metrics port, since `Metric_readers` uses a random port. Note that this flake does **not** reproduce naturally on a developer machine: the window is 0-2 ms locally and does not widen under `taskset -c 0` with `-race` (startup stays around 50-60 ms, below the poll interval), so the unfixed test passes 25/25. To make it deterministic, lower the `waitMetricsReady` tick from `100*time.Millisecond` to `time.Nanosecond`, which opens the same window a slow runner does: - before this change: fails 100% of runs, with the same signature as the CI failures (`metric_stability_test.go:234` `connection refused`, plus the `:219` `operation was canceled` line) - after this change: 10/10 pass, including under `-race` Also run on the unmodified tick: `go test -race -count=3 ./...` and `make -C internal/e2e lint`, both clean. #### Documentation None. Test-only change. #### Authorship - [x] I, a human, wrote this pull request description myself.

signals.title: [featuregate] Emit stable/deprecated gate warnings through the config…
signals.text: #### Description `Registry.Set()` no longer writes stable/deprecated feature gate warnings directly to stdout via `fmt.Printf`. Instead, warnings are buffered on the registry and exposed through a new `Registry.Warnings()` API. The collector drains these buffered warnings during `setupConfigurationComponents`, once the configured logger is available, and emits them as structured warning logs alongside the existing buffered logger output. This keeps the `featuregate` package free of a logging dependency while ensuring warnings are captured by the collector's configured logging pipeline. #### Link to tracking issue Fixes #15586 #### Testing * Added `TestRegistrySetWarnings` to verify that stable and deprecated feature gate warnings are buffered and that `Warnings()` drains the buffer. * Added `TestCollectorFlushesFeatureGateWarnings` to verify buffered warnings are emitted through the collector's configured logger as warning-level log entries. * Ran `go test ./...` for both `featuregate` and `otelcol` packages. * Ran `go vet ./...` for both packages. #### Documentation * Added a changelog entry under `.chloggen`. * No user-facing documentation changes were required since this is an internal logging behavior change. #### Authorship * [x] I, a human, wrote this pull request description myself.

signals.title: [confmap] Remove dead isStringyStructure and add regression test
signals.text: #### Description The bug reported in the tracking issue (a slice of structs with a plain `string` field failing to decode when an env var expands to a value that parses as a number, e.g. `SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN=12345`) was already fixed on `main` by prior work (#14413, #14617, #15339), which changed `useExpandValue()` to check each target field's own type directly instead of relying on an upfront structural walk via `isStringyStructure()`. That stabilization work removed the code path that called `isStringyStructure()`, but left the function itself behind in `confmap/internal/decoder.go` with no remaining callers outside of its own dedicated unit test. This PR removes that dead code and its orphaned test, and adds a regression test that reproduces the exact scenario from the tracking issue to guard against future regressions. This is a dead-code cleanup and test-coverage addition, not a behavioral bug fix — the underlying bug was already resolved before this change. #### Link to tracking issue Fixes # #### Testing Ran, from `confmap/`: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `go test ./...` (all packages, including `confmap/internal`) — all passed. Separately ran `go test ./...` in `confmap/internal/e2e` (its own `go.mod`) — passed. Before making any edits, confirmed via a throwaway reproduction test that the original issue's scenario (slice of struct, plain string field, numeric-valued expanded env var) already decodes correctly on `main`, proving the underlying bug is fixed and this change is purely cleanup plus regression coverage. Also confirmed via `grep` across the whole repository that `isStringyStructure` has no remaining callers after removal. Added `TestExpandedValueInStructSlice` in `confmap/internal/confmap_test.go`, which reproduces the tracking issue's exact scenario and fails without the fix already present on `main` (i.e. it would have caught the original bug had it existed before #14413/#14617/#15339). #### Documentation No documentation changes — this is an internal, unexported code path with no user-facing behavior change. #### Authorship - [ ] I, a human, wrote this pull request description myself. <!--Please delete paragraphs that you did not use before submitting.--> --- AI assistance: this change was drafted with Claude Code. signals.title: fix(memorylimiter): report health status only on state changes
signals.text: #### Description The `memory_limiter` processor currently reports a `StatusOK` event on every memory check while memory usage remains below the soft limit. Since `CheckMemLimits()` runs periodically, this can generate repeated health status events even when the component remains in the same healthy state. This changes the recovery path so that: - `StatusRecoverableError` is reported when the memory limiter enters the refusing state. - `StatusOK` is reported when the memory limiter recovers from the refusing state - no status event is reported while the component remains in the same state. <!-- Issue number if applicable --> #### Link to tracking issue Fixes #15751 <!--Describe what testing was performed and which tests were added.--> #### Testing The above changes were tested with `go test ./internal/memorylimiter`. <!--Describe the documentation added.--> #### Documentation <!--Authorship attestation. signals.title: [chore][cmd/mdatagen] fix confmap import in resource test generation template
signals.text: ### Description #### The Bug The template to generate `resource_test.go` files is currently hardcoded to import from `go.opentelemetry.io/confmap/xconfmap`, but recently, all references in this file were changed from `xconfmap` to `confmap` (see: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/pull/15618). On contrib, this is causing an issue while developing components with `override_value_enabled: true`. Their generated tests currently use the correct `confmap` import (Otelbot [automatically updated them](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/pull/49809/changes#diff-b04954c2f1ae32692ebea806ba15c308d03de440158ea1a54abe247ff8ea09fbL10-R10)), but running `make mdatagen` reverts it back to to the old `xconfmap`, causing compilation errors. #### Steps for Reproduction 1. On contrib, Run `make mdatagen` against `receiver/sqlserverreceiver`, `oracledbreceiver`, `mysqlreceiver` or `postgresqlreceiver` 2. Alternatively, you can run `mdatagen` against its own `samplescraper` and observe the import change. #### The Fix This PR updates the import in the template. ### Link to tracking issue Tangentially related to https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/pull/15613 ### Testing 1. signals.title: [chore][sharedcomponent] Fix lifecycle status duplication and start-error propagation
signals.text: <!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue. Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.--> #### Description The `sharedcomponent` wrapper reported its own lifecycle statuses (`Starting`, `Stopping`, etc), which duplicated the lifecycle statuses reported in the component graph. The original reason for this was intentional, but is no longer needed as of #10777 (see https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/14692#issuecomment-5286069213 for details). The duplicates were harmless because the state machine discarded them as invalid self-transitions. This change makes the graph the single source of lifecycle status. `sharedcomponent` reports and routes runtime statuses to each instance. It also returns the start error on every `Start()` call rather than only the first, so a shared component that fails to start reports the failure to every pipeline that shares it. There is no user-observable behavior change: the previous duplicate/omitted events were discarded by the state machine, and the missing start error is currently hidden by the graph aborting on the first start failure. <!-- Issue number if applicable --> #### Link to tracking issue Fixes #14692 <!--Describe what testing was performed and which tests were added.--> #### Testing - Units / manual <!--Authorship attestation. signal.title: [exporter/otlp_http] Prevent retries when body parsing fails on successful HTTP exports
signal.text: ### Description Fixes an issue in the `otlp_http` exporter where successful (2xx) HTTP response bodies exceeding the 64kB limit (`maxHTTPResponseReadBytes`) triggered retry loops. To resolve this, any error encountered while reading or parsing a successful (2xx) response body is now wrapped and returned as a permanent error (`consumererror.NewPermanent(err)`). This ensures the exporter drops the batch and does not attempt to retry. ### Link to tracking issue Fixes #15386 ### Testing - Added a new unit test `TestPartialSuccess_responseBodyTooLarge` in `exporter/otlphttpexporter/otlp_test.go` verifying that a partial success response exceeding 64kB returns a permanent error. - Ran all package tests successfully using `go test -v ./...` and `make test`. - Ran linter validation successfully using `make lint`. ### Documentation No documentation changes are required. ### Authorship - [x] I, a human, wrote this pull request description myself.

signal.title: [chore][sharedcomponent] Fix lifecycle status duplication and start-error propagation
signal.text: <!--Ex. Fixing a bug - Describe the bug and how this fixes the issue. Ex. Adding a feature - Explain what this achieves.--> #### Description The `sharedcomponent` wrapper reported its own lifecycle statuses (`Starting`, `Stopping`, etc), which duplicated the lifecycle statuses reported in the component graph. The original reason for this was intentional, but is no longer needed as of #10777 (see https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/14692#issuecomment-5286069213 for details). The duplicates were harmless because the state machine discarded them as invalid self-transitions. This change makes the graph the single source of lifecycle status. `sharedcomponent` reports and routes runtime statuses to each instance. It also returns the start error on every `Start()` call rather than only the first, so a shared component that fails to start reports the failure to every pipeline that shares it. There is no user-observable behavior change: the previous duplicate/omitted events were discarded by the state machine, and the missing start error is currently hidden by the graph aborting on the first start failure. <!-- Issue number if applicable --> #### Link to tracking issue Fixes #14692 <!--Describe what testing was performed and which tests were added.--> #### Testing - Units / manual <!--Authorship attestation. signal.title: [service/telemetry] Route OTel SDK internal errors through the collec…
signal.text: When service.telemetry.logs.encoding: json is configured, most collector logs are JSON, but internal OTel SDK errors (e.g. failed metric exports) were emitted via the default OTel global error handler, which uses stdlib log.Print and produces non-JSON lines that break log pipelines expecting uniform JSON. Registers otel.SetErrorHandler in createLogger so these errors are routed through the collector's configured zap logger instead. Fixes #12378 <!--Ex. signal.title: [confmap] Remove dead isStringyStructure and add regression test
signal.text: #### Description The bug reported in the tracking issue (a slice of structs with a plain `string` field failing to decode when an env var expands to a value that parses as a number, e.g. `SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN=12345`) was already fixed on `main` by prior work (#14413, #14617, #15339), which changed `useExpandValue()` to check each target field's own type directly instead of relying on an upfront structural walk via `isStringyStructure()`. That stabilization work removed the code path that called `isStringyStructure()`, but left the function itself behind in `confmap/internal/decoder.go` with no remaining callers outside of its own dedicated unit test. This PR removes that dead code and its orphaned test, and adds a regression test that reproduces the exact scenario from the tracking issue to guard against future regressions. This is a dead-code cleanup and test-coverage addition, not a behavioral bug fix — the underlying bug was already resolved before this change. #### Link to tracking issue Fixes # #### Testing Ran, from `confmap/`: `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `go test ./...` (all packages, including `confmap/internal`) — all passed. Separately ran `go test ./...` in `confmap/internal/e2e` (its own `go.mod`) — passed. Before making any edits, confirmed via a throwaway reproduction test that the original issue's scenario (slice of struct, plain string field, numeric-valued expanded env var) already decodes correctly on `main`, proving the underlying bug is fixed and this change is purely cleanup plus regression coverage. Also confirmed via `grep` across the whole repository that `isStringyStructure` has no remaining callers after removal. Added `TestExpandedValueInStructSlice` in `confmap/internal/confmap_test.go`, which reproduces the tracking issue's exact scenario and fails without the fix already present on `main` (i.e. it would have caught the original bug had it existed before #14413/#14617/#15339). #### Documentation No documentation changes — this is an internal, unexported code path with no user-facing behavior change. #### Authorship - [ ] I, a human, wrote this pull request description myself. <!--Please delete paragraphs that you did not use before submitting.--> --- AI assistance: this change was drafted with Claude Code. Fixes #12793

signal.title: [confmap] is not preserving the original type when a slice of a map is unmarshalled
signal.text: ### Component(s) confmap ### What happened? **Describe the bug** When using an env variable with numerical values, example: `SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN=12345` ```` extensions: headers_setter: headers: - action: upsert key: X-SF-TOKEN from_context: X-SF-TOKEN default_value: "${SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN}" ```` the collector fails to start with the below error: ```` Error: failed to get config: cannot unmarshal the configuration: decoding failed due to the following error(s): error decoding 'extensions': error reading configuration for "headers_setter": decoding failed due to the following error(s): 'headers[0].default_value' expected type 'string', got unconvertible type 'int', value: '12345' ```` **Steps to reproduce** Set the env variable to `SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN=12345` and run contrib using a config like this: ```` extensions: headers_setter: headers: - action: upsert key: X-SF-TOKEN from_context: X-SF-TOKEN default_value: "${SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN}" receivers: hostmetrics: collection_interval: 10s scrapers: filesystem: memory: processors: batch: batch/out: metadata_keys: - X-SF-Token exporters: otlphttp: metrics_endpoint: https://ingest.us1.signalfx.com/v2/datapoint/otlp headers: X-SF-Token: "${SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN}" auth: authenticator: headers_setter service: telemetry: logs: level: "info" pipelines: metrics/internal: receivers: [hostmetrics] processors: [batch] exporters: [otlphttp] extensions: [headers_setter] ```` **What did you expect to see?** No error **What did you see instead?** Below error ```` Error: failed to get config: cannot unmarshal the configuration: decoding failed due to the following error(s): error decoding 'extensions': error reading configuration for "headers_setter": decoding failed due to the following error(s): 'headers[0].default_value' expected type 'string', got unconvertible type 'int', value: '12345' ```` What I believe is happening is that the confmap correctly handles maps and run each entry of the map into the `isStringyStructure`, however, when a config is made out of a slice of maps is used (like the case here), the decoder hooks do not run each entry of the slice into `isStringyStructure` . ### Collector version main ### Environment information ## Environment OS: (e.g., "Ubuntu 20.04") Compiler(if manually compiled): (e.g., "go 14.2") ### OpenTelemetry Collector configuration ```yaml extensions: headers_setter: headers: - X-SF-Token exporters: otlphttp: metrics_endpoint: https://ingest.us1.signalfx.com/v2/datapoint/otlp headers: X-SF-Token: "${SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN}" auth: authenticator: headers_setter service: telemetry: logs: level: "info" pipelines: metrics/internal: receivers: [hostmetrics] processors: [batch] exporters: [otlphttp] extensions: [headers_setter] ``` ### Log output ```shell ``` ### Additional context _No response_

signal.title: Components using sharedcomponent may emit invalid status sequences
signal.text: ### Component(s) https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/tree/main/internal/sharedcomponent ### Describe the issue you're reporting > [!IMPORTANT] > The effects of this issue are completely hidden by the status state machine discarding invalid status transitions. I'm filing it for reference, as it came up while working on #14282. Shared components need to report status differently than normal components to avoid duplication and race conditions. The [implementation](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/a1eb0cadf34bcbeb20d483e5f18e1da0325ba1f1/internal/sharedcomponent/sharedcomponent.go#L87) claims it does this, but in practice has several issues which are hidden by the [status finite state machine](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/80269724f45ae2b17bca7bb533d05c577b33aa8d/service/internal/status/status.go#L50). #### Component start and shutdown statuses are reported twice The implementation claims it takes over from the component graph, but this isn't true. `Graph.StartAll` [always reports](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/80269724f45ae2b17bca7bb533d05c577b33aa8d/service/internal/graph/graph.go#L427) `Starting`, `OK` and `PermanentError` if needed. This duplicates the statuses already reported by the sharedcomponent wrapper. #### The graph may report a Starting status after the actual component emits a different one Sharedcomponent starts the actual component on the first call to `Start()`, and the component will start running immediately, and can immediately report statuses. These are correctly routed and retained for components which are started later, but the graph will still emit `Starting` for those components - despite the component already running and emitting its own statuses. #### Permanent errors are only returned on the first call to `Start()` Subsequent calls return `nil`. Currently, this isn't a problem because the graph will abort on first error, but it will become a problem if we want to change that behavior in the future. ### Tip <sub>[React](https://github.blog/news-insights/product-news/add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) with 👍 to help prioritize this issue. Please use comments to provide useful context, avoiding `+1` or `me too`, to help us triage it. Learn more [here](https://opentelemetry.io/community/end-user/issue-participation/).</sub>

The main reason for this release is compatibility with the new lychee `0.24.x` release artifacts. Starting with lychee `v0.24.0`, the archive layout changed, and the `lychee` binary may now be packaged inside a subdirectory. `lychee-action` now detects that layout automatically, so users can upgrade without changing their workflows. If you use: ```yaml uses: lycheeverse/lychee-action@v2 ``` you will get the new version once the floating `v2` tag has been updated. If you pin exact versions, update to: ```yaml uses: lycheeverse/lychee-action@v2.9.0 ``` #### What’s new from lychee `v0.24.x` ##### Better diagnostics lychee now reports line and column numbers for detected links. This makes broken link reports easier to act on, especially in larger documentation sites or generated reports. ##### Text fragment checking lychee can now check URL text fragments, such as links containing `#:~:text=...`. This helps catch links that point to a valid page but no longer points to the intended highlighted text. ##### Sitemap support lychee can now read `sitemap.xml` inputs. This is useful for checking published websites or generated documentation sites where the sitemap is the easiest source of URLs to validate. ##### JUnit output lychee now supports JUnit output. This makes it easier to integrate link checking results with CI systems and test reporting tools that understand JUnit XML. ##### Redirect and remap visibility lychee can now show redirects and remaps more clearly. This helps explain why a URL was checked as a different final URL and makes debugging link-checking behavior easier. ##### Multiple config files lychee now supports multiple configuration files and expanded config handling. This is useful for repositories that split documentation, website, or package-specific link-checking settings. ##### Timeout handling lychee can now accept timeouts explicitly. This gives users more control over how strict their link checks should be for flaky or slow endpoints. #### Fixes and reliability improvements ##### Fixed lychee `0.24.x` archive compatibility `lychee-action` now handles the new lychee release archive layout by detecting whether the `lychee` binary is inside a subdirectory. This fixes compatibility with lychee `0.24.x`. ##### More stable installation path The action now installs lychee into `$RUNNER_TEMP/lychee/bin` instead of `$HOME`. This avoids failures on runners where `$HOME` differs between composite action steps. In those environments, the action could add one directory to `PATH` but install the binary somewhere else, causing `lychee: command not found`. ##### Safer automatic lychee version updates The workflow that checks for new lychee releases now guards against `null` release versions before creating update PRs. This prevents invalid automated PRs such as “Update lycheeVersion to null”. ##### Dependency updates - Updated `actions/checkout` from `v6` to `v7` - Updated `actions/cache` from `v5` to `v6` #### Upstream lychee changelog For the full lychee changelog, see: - signal.title: fix(memorylimiter): report health status only on state changes
signal.text: #### Description The `memory_limiter` processor currently reports a `StatusOK` event on every memory check while memory usage remains below the soft limit. Since `CheckMemLimits()` runs periodically, this can generate repeated health status events even when the component remains in the same healthy state. This changes the recovery path so that: - `StatusRecoverableError` is reported when the memory limiter enters the refusing state. - `StatusOK` is reported when the memory limiter recovers from the refusing state - no status event is reported while the component remains in the same state. <!-- Issue number if applicable --> #### Link to tracking issue Fixes #15751 <!--Describe what testing was performed and which tests were added.--> #### Testing The above changes were tested with `go test ./internal/memorylimiter`. <!--Describe the documentation added.--> #### Documentation <!--Authorship attestation. signal.title: [processor/memorylimiter] Only send component status events when status changed
signal.text: ### Component(s) processor/memorylimiter ### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe. Now that `memory_limiter` processor reports component status, it can result in a lot of health check events being generated. An event is generated with each check, even when there is no change in status. This can create a lot of noise since the memory_limiter is typically running quite frequently (e.g. recommended default `check_interval` is 1s). This can increases load/impact on the downstream consumers of health events. https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/885b51bf8959315048480c9b1856c605a779b7ec/internal/memorylimiter/memorylimiter.go#L267-L275 ### Describe the solution you'd like Only report the health event status when the state has changed ### Describe alternatives you've considered _No response_ ### Additional context _No response_ ### Tip <sub>[React](https://github.blog/news-insights/product-news/add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) with 👍 to help prioritize this issue. signal.title: [chore][cmd/mdatagen] fix confmap import in resource test generation template
signal.text: ### Description #### The Bug The template to generate `resource_test.go` files is currently hardcoded to import from `go.opentelemetry.io/confmap/xconfmap`, but recently, all references in this file were changed from `xconfmap` to `confmap` (see: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/pull/15618). On contrib, this is causing an issue while developing components with `override_value_enabled: true`. Their generated tests currently use the correct `confmap` import (Otelbot [automatically updated them](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/pull/49809/changes#diff-b04954c2f1ae32692ebea806ba15c308d03de440158ea1a54abe247ff8ea09fbL10-R10)), but running `make mdatagen` reverts it back to to the old `xconfmap`, causing compilation errors. #### Steps for Reproduction 1. On contrib, Run `make mdatagen` against `receiver/sqlserverreceiver`, `oracledbreceiver`, `mysqlreceiver` or `postgresqlreceiver` 2. Run `make tidy && make gci` Result: In `generated_resource_test.go`, the import `go.opentelemetry.io/collector/confmap` reverts to `go.opentelemetry.io/collector/xconfmap`, causing an `import not used` error. Alternatively, you can run `mdatagen` against its own `samplescraper` and observe the import change. #### The Fix This PR updates the import in the template. ### Link to tracking issue Tangentially related to https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/pull/15613 ### Testing 1. Installed this version of mdatagen using `go install` 2. Against `sqlserverreceiver` and other components, ran `make mdatagen MDATAGEN=<local_binary>` and `make tidy && make gci` 3. Observed import no longer reverts ### Authorship - [x] I, a human, wrote this pull request description myself.

signal.title: [confighttp] Move keepalive config into a dedicated optional section
signal.text: #### Description Move the keepalive-related options into a dedicated optional section. We go from: ```yaml endpoint: "http://localhost:4318" idle_conn_timeout: 90s max_idle_conns: 100 max_idle_conns_per_host: 10 ``` to: ```yaml endpoint: "http://localhost:4318" keepalive: idle_conn_timeout: 90s max_idle_conns: 100 max_idle_conns_per_host: 10 ``` The old configuration still exists and works. We fail validation if both are set. The implementation is somewhat complex and tries to minimize breakage across multiple scenarios. It proceeds by standardizing on the old, deprecated fields in `Unmarshal` and nulling the new section. See comments on the `Unmarshal` implementation and compatibility tests in `keepalive_compat_tests.go`. The most notable scenario that doesn't work goes like this: ```go cfg := NewDefaultClientConfig() conf.Unmarshal(cfg) cfg.KeepAlive = nil client := cfg.ToClient() ``` Keepalives will be enabled for such a client. This, and other limitations, exist as tests in `keepalive_compat_test.go`. Their intent is to show how a given implementation fares, in case somebody can come up with a better one. #### Link to tracking issue Fixes https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/14020 #### Testing Added unit tests for all the new functions and some more generic unmarshalling tests. I've also added compatibility tests in `keepalive_compat_test.go` which assert that typical use cases from contrib still work as expected, and also show the limitations of this approach. I'm open to dropping some of them after review, but I think they're very useful until we decide on an approach. <!--Describe the documentation added.--> #### Documentation Updated README and the config schema.

signal.title: [cmd/mdatagen] [filter] Allow wildcard patterns as a filtering option
signal.text: ### Component(s) cmd/mdatagen ### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe. The `filter` package has a config with two fields: `strict`, and `regexp`. This allows filtering based on string literals or Go regexes. This filter config could be used to address [the desire to mass enable/disable metrics in `MetricsBuilder`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/issues/10074). But using a regex pattern is pretty cumbersome when OTel names are expected to be separated with `.`, which is a regex operator. ### Describe the solution you'd like The [Go metric SDK for Views accepts a simple wildcard pattern](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/blob/91fcbbd0066dba7163ee29f6a2eb7c17a49e0975/sdk/metric/view.go#L71-L77) only supporting `*` (multi-character) and `?` (single-character) wildcards. A new field could be added to filter called `pattern` that would accept this format in the same way. ### Describe alternatives you've considered We could stick to just allowing regexes. I suppose it wouldn't be the end of the world. Using this pattern would just be a significantly nicer config experience in my opinion. ### Additional context _No response_ ### Tip <sub>[React](https://github.blog/news-insights/product-news/add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) with 👍 to help prioritize this issue. signal.title: [featuregate] Emit stable/deprecated gate warnings through the config…
signal.text: #### Description `Registry.Set()` no longer writes stable/deprecated feature gate warnings directly to stdout via `fmt.Printf`. Instead, warnings are buffered on the registry and exposed through a new `Registry.Warnings()` API. The collector drains these buffered warnings during `setupConfigurationComponents`, once the configured logger is available, and emits them as structured warning logs alongside the existing buffered logger output. This keeps the `featuregate` package free of a logging dependency while ensuring warnings are captured by the collector's configured logging pipeline. #### Link to tracking issue Fixes #15586 #### Testing * Added `TestRegistrySetWarnings` to verify that stable and deprecated feature gate warnings are buffered and that `Warnings()` drains the buffer. * Added `TestCollectorFlushesFeatureGateWarnings` to verify buffered warnings are emitted through the collector's configured logger as warning-level log entries. * Ran `go test ./...` for both `featuregate` and `otelcol` packages. * Ran `go vet ./...` for both packages. #### Documentation * Added a changelog entry under `.chloggen`. * No user-facing documentation changes were required since this is an internal logging behavior change. #### Authorship * [x] I, a human, wrote this pull request description myself.

signal.title: feat: add support for identity compression algorithm in confighttp
signal.text: #### Description Per RFC 7231 3.1.2.2, `Content-Encoding: identity` is a valid header value that signifies no encoding/compression was used. The `httpContentDecompressor` previously rejected payloads with `Content-Encoding: identity` with a `400 Bad Request` because `"identity"` was not registered in the available decoders. This PR fixes the issue by mapping `"identity"` to act as a pass-through (identical to `""`) whenever uncompressed payloads are allowed. This also resolves a documented `// BUG:` in the `compression_test.go` suite. #### Link to tracking issue Fixes # #### Testing - Updated the `Mixed_Identity_ShouldAccept` test case in `compression_test.go` which previously expected a `400 Bad Request` (marked as a BUG) to correctly expect `200 OK`. - Ran `go test ./...` in `config/confighttp` and verified all tests pass. #### Documentation None needed. #### Authorship - [x] I, a human, wrote this pull request description myself.

signal.title: fix(service): prevent deadlock when reporting fatal errors during shutdown
signal.text: Ran into this while reviewing shutdown behavior for #9824. The problem is that during shutdown, startup, or config reload the collector control loop is not actively reading from asyncErrorChannel. If a component goroutine calls NotifyComponentStatusChange with a fatal error, the unbuffered channel send blocks forever, deadlocking the caller. I went with a non-blocking select (with default) rather than buffering the channel, because buffering would change the semantics for the normal running case and could mask real errors. With this approach the send succeeds when the control loop is listening, and is silently dropped otherwise, which is the safest behavior during shutdown. Not 100% sure if there is a better way to surface the dropped error, feedback welcome. Fixes #9824

signal.title: [chore][internal/e2e] Wait for the collector to be running before sending data
signal.text: #### Description `TestMetricStability` and `TestInternalTelemetry_ServiceInstanceID` treat a successful scrape of the telemetry `/metrics` endpoint as "the collector is ready". It is not. The meter provider — and with it the Prometheus HTTP server — is created in `service.New` ([`service.go:194`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/0ffbf34b9/service/service.go#L194)). The OTLP receiver only starts much later, in `service.Start` -> `Pipelines.StartAll` ([`service.go:274`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/0ffbf34b9/service/service.go#L274)). Between those two points `/metrics` answers `200` while nothing is listening on the OTLP port, so `waitMetricsReady` returns early and the following `sendTestData` fails with `connect: connection refused`. The window spans `CreateTracerProvider` and `graph.Build` ([`service.go:378`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/0ffbf34b9/service/service.go#L378)), which instantiates every component — cheap on a developer machine, expensive under `-race` on a loaded CI runner. The CI logs confirm this directly. In job `91217674049` the captured output for the failing subtest contains `Internal trace telemetry disabled` (logged by `CreateTracerProvider`, `service.go:209`) but no `Starting otelcol...` — the first line of `service.Start` — anywhere in the log. The collector was inside the window when the test sent data. The `cannot start pipelines: failed to start "otlp" receiver: listen tcp: lookup localhost: operation was canceled` line in #15492 is a consequence rather than the cause: `require.NoError` in `sendTestData` calls `FailNow`, which runs `runtime.Goexit`, which fires the `defer cancel()` — cancelling the context that `confignet.TCPAddrConfig.Listen` is resolving `localhost` under. This PR waits for `Collector.GetState() == StateRunning`, which is set after `service.Start` returns. That is a sound readiness signal because `ToListener(ctx)` is called synchronously inside `startHTTPServer` ([`otlp.go:171`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/blob/0ffbf34b9/receiver/otlpreceiver/otlp.go#L171)) — only `Serve` is backgrounded — so the socket is bound and accepting before `Start` returns. It also surfaces a startup failure through a channel instead of logging it from a goroutine. The previous `t.Logf`/`assert.NoError` calls could run after the test had finished, which panics with `Log in goroutine after test has completed` and would mask the real error. The same defect and the same fix apply to `TestInternalTelemetry_ServiceInstanceID`, which showed up in the same CI sweep. #### Link to tracking issue Fixes #15492 #### Testing `TestMetricStability` accounted for 13 of the 20 most recent failed `build-and-test` runs at the time of writing, across both subtests. That both subtests fail rules out the hardcoded `8888` metrics port, since `Metric_readers` uses a random port. Note that this flake does **not** reproduce naturally on a developer machine: the window is 0-2 ms locally and does not widen under `taskset -c 0` with `-race` (startup stays around 50-60 ms, below the poll interval), so the unfixed test passes 25/25. To make it deterministic, lower the `waitMetricsReady` tick from `100*time.Millisecond` to `time.Nanosecond`, which opens the same window a slow runner does: - before this change: fails 100% of runs, with the same signature as the CI failures (`metric_stability_test.go:234` `connection refused`, plus the `:219` `operation was canceled` line) - after this change: 10/10 pass, including under `-race` Also run on the unmodified tick: `go test -race -count=3 ./...` and `make -C internal/e2e lint`, both clean. #### Documentation None. Test-only change. #### Authorship - [x] I, a human, wrote this pull request description myself.
